This is a one-year internship with intent to hire, and a rare opportunity to own a high-visibility project from day one and directly shape how the team defines, plans, and delivers agentic use cases. You won’t just be analyzing requirements; you’ll uncover patterns in how functional work moves through our system, run the agile cadence that gets it delivered, and turn what you learn into solutions the Technical Owner and Functional Lead will act on. Jira Story Preparation: Based on direction from the Technical Owner, decompose requirements into well-structured Jira epics and stories with clear descriptions, acceptance criteria, and dependencies, so the team has sufficient clarity to execute. Milestone & Deliverable Tracking: Set and track milestones for the requirement-to-delivery pipeline (requirement → breakdown → task → done), flagging slippage early and keeping the Technical Owner informed with concise, accurate status updates. Stakeholder Alignment: Align stakeholders across workstreams; Product Owner, Technical Lead, Functional Lead, and engineering; on scope, sequencing, and dependencies. Program Documentation: Document your approach, decisions, and findings in Confluence so the program’s knowledge stays accessible and current. jobs.description: ABOUT RAMP Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. ABOUT THE ROLE You will build and run the operating systems that help Juno ship reliably and support customers as we scale. On the product operations side, you will turn product decisions into clear operating plans, maintain visibility in Linear, coordinate customer testing and launch readiness, keep commitments and risks visible, and make sure product changes are communicated clearly. You will partner closely with product and engineering to make decisions executable, keep work organized, surface gaps and dependencies, and ensure the team follows through on what it has committed to ship. On the customer support side, you will be the first line of defense when customers encounter product issues. You will triage and investigate problems, coordinate the right response, and redirect travel-service questions to our travel partners. Because you sit close to both the product process and the customer, you will turn recurring friction into clear insights, accountable follow-up, and better operating systems. Success means Juno ships through a lightweight and dependable process, customers understand what changed, risks and commitments do not get lost, recurring issues reach the right owners, and support demand does not grow one-for-one with the business. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Provide holistic support through the entire launch lifecycle across program management, customer testing, launch readiness, change management, customer communication, and post-launch iteration. Own and improve Juno's shipping process so the right reviews, testing, documentation, internal enablement, and customer updates happen at the right time. - Maintain Linear as a reliable operating system for projects, owners, milestones, dependencies, status, and product decisions. Surface risks early and follow through until they are resolved. - Serve as the first line of defense for product-related customer issues across email and chat, join customer calls when needed, manage escalations to resolution, and route travel-service questions to the right partner. - Be the voice of the customer in product decisions. Analyze support trends and customer feedback, diagnose recurring friction, size the problems you find, and translate messy input into clear findings, recommended actions, prioritization input, and accountable follow-up for product and engineering. - Build AI-powered workflows, automations, knowledge systems, and self-service experiences that improve the quality and speed of product operations and customer support. WHAT YOU NEED - 3+ years of experience in product operations, program management, customer experience, technical support, consulting, or another customer-facing analytical role in a fast-moving software company. - You are highly process-oriented. jobs.title: QA Engineer
jobs.description: Hi! I'm [Shriya](https://www.linkedin.com/in/shriya-baddula-4b0b41386), and I lead QA at Ashby. We're hiring a QA Engineer to help us test and strengthen the quality of our product. I think of QA as something you build into the system, not as something you layer on top for added confidence. I'm not interested in gatekeeping quality or creating a process for its own sake. I care about feedback that's fast and useful, the kind engineers trust, and catching the problems users would actually notice. That's what brought me to Ashby. Engineers take on a lot of ownership, including the quality of their work, which often means they test it themselves. QA here isn't about convincing people to care or taking quality off their plate. It's about being another set of eyes on a fast-evolving product. Sometimes that means seeing the edge case. Sometimes that means spotting the product's blind spot before it hits production. In this role, you'll decide what to test, when to test, and which product areas are worth automating. We're a small team, so the work is mixed. We all roll up our sleeves when needed. **Most of your time, roughly 70%, is hands-on manual testing.** You'll work with engineers and other stakeholders on features as they ship, reproduce bugs reported by customers, and, for larger launches, coordinate testing across an entire feature area. The other 30% is automation. You'll write Playwright end-to-end tests and help expand test coverage. You do not need to be an SDET, and you do not need to have built a framework from scratch. **You do need to be comfortable writing code**, reading someone else's code, and getting better at both. If you've written some E2E tests and want to write more, that's the right starting point. We have an existing Playwright suite and page object structure you'll build on, and SDETs who will pair with you and help you grow. What Ashby gives you in return is the best of both early and growth-stage environments. The agency and no-nonsense of a seed startup: you decide what to test, work directly with the people building it, and operate in an almost-no-meeting culture. The product-market fit and scale of a growth-stage startup: 100,000+ weekly active users who depend on our software, which means the things you catch actually matter. We have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet. ### **Why You Should or Shouldn’t Apply** - You have strong product instincts. You test like a user and know the difference between "it works" and "it works the way someone would actually use it." - You're good at reproducing bugs. When something is broken, you narrow it down. You don't file vague bugs and move on. - You are self-sufficient and can scope your own work. Given a feature and a spec, you decide what's worth testing and what’s not, and you know when to ask for help when something is taking too long. - You want to grow on the automation side. You don't need to be an expert to be interested. You want to write more tests, get faster at it, and learn from the engineers around you. - You write clearly. Your writing should be concise, clear, and easy to follow. ### **Put Another Way, You Shouldn't Apply If** - You think of QA as gatekeeping. We don't have sign-off gates, and we're not adding them. Your influence comes from the quality of your judgment, not from a checkbox. - You're happiest when someone hands you a test plan and a set of instructions. This role operates on ownership, with you often deciding what to test and why. - You want to stay at the surface. Testing Ashby well means understanding it well. jobs.description: Join Vetcove and help modernize the future of veterinary software and the pet parent healthcare experience. Our suite of platforms features a market-leading procurement marketplace, an ultra-modern home delivery ecommerce experience, and a next-generation practice management system. More than 25,000 hospitals across all 50 states rely on Vetcove daily, supporting tens of thousands of veterinarians who care for tens of millions of pets each year. We are modernizing the 50 billion dollar plus animal health industry by giving veterinary organizations the tools to focus more on patient care. Backed by Y Combinator and top venture investors in Silicon Valley, New York and Miami, Vetcove is a fast-growing, mission-driven company. We are searching for talented and passionate people who want to help shape the future of veterinary care. About the Role As an Associate Product Manager at Vetcove, you’ll play a critical role in keeping our product teams running smoothly and efficiently. You’ll sit at the intersection of product, engineering, design, and customer-facing teams — helping translate user feedback into actionable insights, supporting product launches, and ensuring our processes scale as we grow. This is an ideal role for someone who is eager to develop deep operational expertise and grow within a fast-moving, mission-driven company. What You’ll Do Support Product Launches: Partner with product managers, onboarding, and support teams to coordinate go-to-market activities, create training materials, and track feature adoption post-launch. Work with Integration Partners: Coordinate and lead discussions between integration partners and engineering teams and overseeing new integrations. Synthesize User Feedback: Collect and organize qualitative feedback from clinics, pet parents, and internal stakeholders, and surface patterns and themes to inform product decisions. Maintain Product Documentation: Draft and maintain product requirement documents, user stories, release notes, and internal process guides to ensure clarity across teams. Track & Report on KPIs: Monitor product performance dashboards, flag anomalies, and compile regular reports to help product managers stay on top of key metrics. Coordinate Cross-Functional Workflows: Help manage sprint planning logistics, backlog grooming, and cross-team communication to keep initiatives on track. Support QA Processes: Assist with quality assurance testing, document bugs and edge cases, and help define acceptance criteria alongside product and engineering teams. What We’re Looking For Bachelors Degree 1+ years of experience in product operations, business operations, project coordination, or a related role Strong written and verbal communication skills with exceptional attention to detail Comfort working with data, including experience with spreadsheets, dashboards, or basic analytics tools Highly organized with the ability to juggle multiple workstreams and deadlines in a fast-paced environment Curiosity about technology and a desire to understand how software products are built and used Bonus: exposure to SaaS products, healthcare or veterinary tech, or customer-facing roles The typical base pay range for this role across the U.S. is: $70,000/year -$110,000/year + bonus + equity + benefits. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations. For Colorado, the salary range is: $75,000 - $105,000 + bonus + equity + benefits. This salary range is a good faith estimate of what Vetcove may pay for this position at the time of posting. Actual compensation may vary based on skills, qualifications, and experience. The range reflects the base hourly rate or annual compensation (as applicable), and does not include bonus, equity or other incentives. In addition to base compensation, Vetcove offers a comprehensive benefits package. Please refer to the “Benefits (Full Time Roles)” section above for more details.
